items.q: Look! The cat ______ on the kitchen table again.
items.vi: Nhìn kìa! Con mèo lại đang ngủ trên bàn bếp.
items.explanation: Look! points to something happening right now, so the present continuous is sleeping is needed, not a simple or perfect form.

items.q: The kitten ______ its paw on a piece of broken glass in the garden.
items.vi: Con mèo con bị đứt chân vì một mảnh thủy tinh vỡ trong vườn.
items.explanation: Broken glass makes a cut. You bruise yourself by knocking against something, and you sprain or strain a joint or muscle by twisting it.

items.q: Everyone expects Tuan's dog to ______ at Sunday's race because it is much faster than the others.
items.vi: Ai cũng nghĩ chó của Tuấn sẽ thắng dễ dàng ở cuộc đua hôm Chủ nhật vì nó nhanh hơn hẳn những con khác.
items.explanation: Win hands down = win very easily. Win by a whisker means win only just, which contradicts 'much faster'; run out of steam and lose its way describe failing.

items.q: You should ______ your promise to visit Grandma this weekend, or she will be very upset.
items.vi: Con nên giữ lời hứa đi thăm bà vào cuối tuần này, không thì bà sẽ buồn lắm.
items.explanation: The collocation is keep a promise (do what you said you would do). Hold, stay and save do not go with promise in this meaning.

items.q: Don't ______ your teammates by missing the school cooking contest on Saturday.
items.vi: Đừng làm đồng đội thất vọng bằng cách bỏ lỡ cuộc thi nấu ăn của trường vào thứ Bảy.
items.explanation: Let somebody down = disappoint someone. Turn down = refuse, let off = not punish, put down = criticise or place something.

items.q: Nobody could explain the reason ______ the school swimming pool stayed closed all summer.
items.vi: Không ai giải thích được lý do vì sao bể bơi của trường đóng cửa suốt cả mùa hè.
items.explanation: After the reason, the relative adverb why is used. Where follows a place, when a time, and which would need to be the subject or object of the clause, which it is not here.

items.q: After eating the fish that had been left out in the sun, Nam felt ______ and had to lie down.
items.vi: Sau khi ăn con cá bị để ngoài nắng, Nam thấy buồn nôn và phải nằm nghỉ.
items.explanation: Bad food makes you feel sick. Sore, bruised and hurt describe a painful part of the body, not a feeling of illness.

items.q: The bowl is empty — the cat ______ all the fish while we were out.
items.vi: Cái bát trống không — chắc chắn con mèo đã ăn hết cá lúc chúng ta đi vắng.
items.explanation: Must have + past participle is a confident guess about the past based on evidence (the empty bowl). Can't have means the opposite; should have and needn't have express advice or lack of need, not deduction.

items.q: Parrots are famous ______ copying the sounds of human speech.
items.vi: Vẹt nổi tiếng vì bắt chước được âm thanh tiếng người.
items.explanation: The adjective famous takes the preposition for before the thing someone is known for; of, about and with do not follow it.

items.q: My grandmother ______ the same soup recipe since she was a little girl.
items.vi: Bà tôi đã dùng cùng một công thức nấu canh này từ khi bà còn là một cô bé.
items.explanation: Since + a past starting point describes something that continues up to now, so the present perfect has used is needed.

items.q: Lan's ankle became ______ after she twisted it on the mountain trail.
items.vi: Cổ chân của Lan bị sưng lên sau khi cô ấy bị trẹo chân trên đường mòn lên núi.
items.explanation: A twisted ankle becomes swollen (bigger than normal). Dizzy, hoarse and feverish describe a person's head, voice or temperature, not a joint.

items.q: Could you ______ the table while I finish the spring rolls?
items.vi: Con dọn bàn ăn giúp mẹ trong lúc mẹ làm nốt chả giò được không?
items.explanation: The collocation is lay the table (put out the plates, bowls and chopsticks). Put, make and do do not go with 'the table' in this meaning.

items.q: Lan: Are we going to the beach tomorrow? / Nam: If the weather ______ fine, we'll take the dog with us.
items.vi: Lan: Mai mình đi biển chứ? / Nam: Nếu trời đẹp, mình sẽ dắt chó theo.
items.explanation: A first conditional uses the present simple in the if-clause and will in the main clause, even when it refers to the future.

items.q: Planting ten trees is only ______ when a whole forest has been cut down.
items.vi: Trồng mười cái cây chỉ như muối bỏ biển khi cả một khu rừng đã bị chặt.
items.explanation: A drop in the ocean = a very small amount compared with what is needed. A piece of cake = very easy; a storm in a teacup = a fuss about nothing; a breath of fresh air = something pleasantly new.

items.q: There is only ______ rice left in the pot, so I'll cook some noodles as well.
items.vi: Trong nồi chỉ còn một ít cơm, nên mình sẽ nấu thêm mì.
items.explanation: Rice is uncountable, so it takes a little. A few, many and several are only used with plural countable nouns.

items.q: Mai has a bad ______, so she keeps coughing and sneezing in class.
items.vi: Mai bị cảm nặng nên cứ ho và hắt hơi liên tục trong lớp.
items.explanation: Coughing and sneezing are the signs of a cold. An ache is a dull pain, a bruise is a dark mark on the skin, and a rash is a patch of red spots.

items.q: Our old dog ______ peacefully last winter, and we buried him under the mango tree.
items.vi: Con chó già của chúng tôi đã qua đời thanh thản vào mùa đông năm ngoái, và chúng tôi chôn nó dưới gốc xoài.
items.explanation: Pass away is a gentle way of saying die. Pass out = faint, pass by = go past, give away = give something as a present.

items.q: The vet said she ______ the problem with our rabbit's teeth the next day.
items.vi: Bác sĩ thú y nói rằng hôm sau cô ấy sẽ xem xét vấn đề về răng của con thỏ nhà chúng tôi.
items.explanation: In reported speech after said, will becomes would: 'I will look into it tomorrow' becomes she would look into it the next day.

items.q: Nam: Shall we eat out tonight? / Lan: I'd rather ______ at home; I've bought some fresh prawns.
items.vi: Nam: Tối nay mình ra ngoài ăn nhé? / Lan: Tớ thích nấu ở nhà hơn; tớ mới mua ít tôm tươi.
items.explanation: Would rather is followed by the bare infinitive: I'd rather cook, not 'to cook', 'cooking' or 'cooked'.

items.q: When I got home from school, my dog ______ my new slippers to pieces.
items.vi: Khi tôi đi học về thì con chó đã cắn nát đôi dép mới của tôi.
items.explanation: The chewing happened before I got home, so the earlier past action takes the past perfect: had chewed. Present forms cannot follow a past time clause here.

items.q: Minh has a terrible ______, so he can't chew the sticky rice cake his mother made.
items.vi: Minh bị đau răng dữ dội nên không nhai được bánh chưng mẹ làm.
items.explanation: Only a toothache stops you chewing. A headache, an earache and a stomachache are pains in other parts of the body.

items.q: Nam loves spicy food, ______ his sister cannot eat even a little chilli.
items.vi: Nam rất thích đồ ăn cay, trong khi chị của cậu ấy không ăn nổi dù chỉ một chút ớt.
items.explanation: Whereas links two contrasting facts. Therefore and so that give a result or purpose, and because gives a reason — none of them fits a contrast.

items.q: Fresh vegetables ______ to the market every morning by farmers from the countryside.
items.vi: Rau tươi được nông dân từ vùng quê chở đến chợ mỗi sáng.
items.explanation: The vegetables do not act; they receive the action, and by farmers shows the agent, so the present simple passive are brought is needed.

items.q: Lan: Why don't you buy frozen fish? It's cheaper. / Nam: Fresh fish tastes far ______ than frozen fish.
items.vi: Lan: Sao cậu không mua cá đông lạnh? Rẻ hơn mà. / Nam: Cá tươi ăn ngon hơn cá đông lạnh nhiều.
items.explanation: Than signals a comparative, and the comparative of good is better; far simply makes the comparison stronger.

items.q: After dinner, Nam always ______ the washing-up so that his mother can rest.
items.vi: Sau bữa tối, Nam luôn rửa bát để mẹ được nghỉ ngơi.
items.explanation: The collocation is do the washing-up, like do the cooking or do the dishes; make, take and get do not go with it.
